sources.title: Two Algorithms for Frequency Estimation of a Real Sinusoid from Short Data Records
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 2000 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS), vol. 3, pp. III-391–III-394
sources.publication_status: Author's publication list identifies it as an IEEE ISCAS 2000 proceedings paper (op10, lines 462-463); the paper PDF carries IEEE copyright. Peer-review status was not independently verified.
sources.access_level: Primary paper PDF opened (op3); full extracted text was returned in search operation op6. Author-hosted access; publisher page was not verified.
sources.content_locator: PDF pp. III-391–III-394; abstract and Section I discuss severe short-record periodogram bias; Section II attributes bias to the negative spectral line and says it depends on N, tone frequency, and phase; Section III proposes analytic-signal construction and negative-line subtraction. Model is one real sinusoid in additive white Gaussian noise with unknown amplitude, frequency and phase; short records are described as N on the order of 100 or less.

findings.claim: A complex-sinusoid/periodogram estimator can have phase- and record-length-dependent bias on a real sampled tone because the tone includes a negative-frequency spectral component. So and Chan propose two concrete corrections: construct an analytic signal, or subtract the negative spectral line before periodogram estimation.
findings.support_locator: Primary paper abstract and Sections I-III, pp. III-391–III-394; extracted paper text returned at op6 and PDF opened at op3.
findings.decision_implication: This identifies a model-mismatch check that could change the next estimator comparison: on matched real-valued tone captures, include a short-window periodogram baseline and one real-tone image-correction method, varying initial phase and record length. Compare frequency bias and deadline error tails; keep presence admission and frequency-only authority scored separately. The work is a comparator/discriminator, not a selected implementation.
assumptions: Real sinusoid with unknown fixed amplitude, phase and frequency over the analyzed record.
Additive white Gaussian noise in the paper's model.
The paper's improvement is specifically motivated for short observation records, including N around 100 or less.
findings.applicability_gap: Supplied H03 identifies real capture and unresolved conjugate-image/physical-sideband ambiguity, so model relevance is direct; actual capture length, tone-to-sample-rate ratio, envelope variation, payload/auxiliary interference and 24/30 dB-Hz operating conditions may fall outside the paper's single-tone AWGN experiments. The source does not establish target feasibility or false-admission behavior.
findings.next_discriminator: Using the same real PCM and noise/control captures, vary start phase and observation length around the actual 137-sample chunk aggregation and longer windows; compare current estimator, real-tone image correction and bounded local fit. Record bias, <=0.10-Hz deadline success, large-error tails, reported uncertainty coverage, and absent-tone publications separately. Repeat with representative envelope/payload activity only after the clean single-tone discriminator isolates the image effect.

incremental_vs_seed.new_evidence: A primary real-sinusoid study names a specific finite-record model failure (negative spectral-line interference) and two executable remedy families, beyond the seed's complex single-tone estimator comparisons and generic coarse-search/outlier discussion.
incremental_vs_seed.seed_claim_or_gap_changed: H03 already flags unresolved conjugate-image/physical-sideband ambiguity. This turns that broad caveat into a testable estimator-bias hypothesis and a small, matched comparison; it does not resolve which branch or estimator performs best on the receiver's captures.

retained_seed_summary: Retain seed findings that CRLB/local uncertainty does not establish deadline tail error (Rife-Boorstyn excerpt, with original-access provenance caveat); Kay-style/ML and differential-phase lag comparisons are conditioned on stationary complex AWGN/coherence; and uncertainty, current presence and frequency-only authority are distinct. H03/H05/H06 are source excerpts and synthetic fixtures, not performance observations on prospective captures.

unresolved: Actual capture sample rates, tone frequency relative to DC/Nyquist, usable coherent record lengths, and amplitude stability determine the size of negative-image bias.
The source assumes AWGN and a stationary single tone; payload, auxiliary tones, shaped/enveloped helper activity, and colored or impulsive interference require matched runtime evidence.
The paper does not calibrate the reported uncertainty field or support 95% deadline success, presence false-admission control, or the hypothetical 6 s / 0.10 Hz target.
Physical positive/negative sideband ambiguity remains separate from estimating the tone's digital frequency.
